newOpportunities.requirements: Works must survive an outdoor Alpine-foothill winter for 11 weeks and integrate with municipal street infrastructure. Pitch as an artwork, not a lighting product. Italian-language materials strongly advised.
newOpportunities.intel: Two doors. (1) info@lucidartistatorino.org and the Ufficio arte e design, via Meucci 4, Turin — an Italian one-pager plus images of realised works. (2) More effective: watch fondazionetorinomusei.it for the periodic avviso per il conferimento dell'incarico di curatela that names the incoming Luci d'Artista curator, then approach that individual in the first months of their term while they build their artist list. New works are unveiled in September and lit in late October, so commissioning happens the preceding winter and spring — pitch January through April. The sphere is the stronger proposal; drones fit an accensione (switch-on) event, not the permanent collection.
newOpportunities.warning: The festival site's contact page is a form only; info@lucidartistatorino.org is published by Città di Torino's scheda rather than the festival site. No individual curator name confirmed for the current term.

newOpportunities.name: Videocittà — Rome digital/audiovisual festival at the Gazometro
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Three days in early-to-mid July at the Gazometro Ostiense; satellites in Naples and L'Aquila; a winter edition also runs
newOpportunities.what: Italy's most significant festival of digital vision and audiovisual culture — immersive installations, video art, large-scale mapping on the Gazometro, VR and live AV. The 9th edition ran 10-12 July 2026 on the theme of water. Works are curated and commissioned, not open-called. It also runs Agorà, an international marketplace for digital creativity drawing 40+ operators from 20 countries — the practical back door for a studio rather than a solo artist.
newOpportunities.selection: Curatorial. Curators Michele Lotti and Anna Lea Antolini; video art by Damiana Leoni and Rä di Martino, under Creative Director Francesco Dobrovich. Programme announced in May for the July edition.
newOpportunities.scale: Three days, industrial-archaeology site, tens of thousands of attendees, plus a professional marketplace strand
newOpportunities.requirements: Indoor and outdoor both viable at the Gazometro. For a drone show, Rome airspace near Ostiense is restricted — arrive with an ENAC-authorised Italian operator identified. The sphere is the lower-friction proposal.
newOpportunities.intel: Do not cold-email info@ and wait. The lever is Guido Pietro Airoldi, International Development & Partnerships — the named business contact whose job is bringing in foreign work and co-producers. Write to him with a one-page treatment and a link, and separately apply as an operator to Agorà, which is how international studios get into the room without a commission first. Giulia Funari (General Organization) is the production contact once something is agreed. Pitch October-January: the July programme is curated over autumn and announced in May.
newOpportunities.warning: Individual staff emails are not published — only info@videocitta.com plus the team list on their corporate-governance page. The note that Agorà accepts external operators comes from press coverage, not a published call.

newOpportunities.name: Constellations de Metz — appel à projets
newOpportunities.org: Ville de Metz / Eurométropole de Metz
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Late June to early September; the 10th edition ran 25 June - 5 September 2026
newOpportunities.what: A free ten-week summer festival splitting into Pierres Numériques (nocturnal digital art and video mapping on Metz's monuments — 11 works, Thu-Sat evenings) and a daytime urban-art trail of 13 works. Unusually for a French light festival it publishes a genuine annual appel à projets, including a mapping competition that selects five candidates for the Cloître des Trinitaires facades, scored 50% aesthetic / 50% thematic relevance.
newOpportunities.selection: Published annual call, applications by email to the city; a jury selects five projects for the mapping strand. The 2025 cycle ran: deadline late February, results mid-March, final files mid-May, opening mid-June.
newOpportunities.scale: Ten-week run, monument facades across central Metz, free entry
newOpportunities.requirements: French-language dossier. The mapping strand is projection-based, not drone; the daytime urban-art strand is where a kinetic light object or the sphere fits. Ten weeks outdoors means weatherproofing and low-maintenance design matter more than spectacle.
newOpportunities.intel: The call is not always advertised outside France — watch metz.fr/actus in December and January, or simply write to constellations@mairie-metz.fr now asking to be added to the appel à projets mailing list. That is the single highest-leverage action here and costs nothing. Request the règlement pack by email — literally how the 2025 call instructed candidates to obtain materials. Pitch the sphere into the urban-art trail and a projection or kinetic work into Pierres Numériques; do not lead with drones.
newOpportunities.warning: No 2027 call published at time of checking — dates, strands and the February deadline are extrapolated from the City of Metz's own published 2023 and 2025 calls.

newOpportunities.name: Mons en Lumières — appel à candidatures artistiques
newOpportunities.eventWindow: 27-31 January 2027; a 3 km illuminated route through the city centre, free entry
newOpportunities.what: The largest light festival in Wallonia, run by the City of Mons (a former European Capital of Culture with real production capacity). A 3 km night trail, five evenings, free. The 2027 edition is themed Créateurs de temps and explicitly sought artists with a strong artistic vision and immersive light installations — their site confirms the 2027 call ran and is complete, which means the same call reopens for 2028.
newOpportunities.selection: Published open call for artists, launched by the Ville de Mons and relayed through Walloon arts networks.
newOpportunities.scale: Five evenings, 3 km route, city-centre squares and heritage buildings, tens of thousands of visitors
newOpportunities.requirements: French-language application. January in Belgium is cold and wet — the weatherproofed sphere is the natural fit; the drone piece would be positioned as a nightly trail finale, and Belgian drone display over an urban centre requires a BCAA/Skeyes-cleared operator.
newOpportunities.intel: The 2027 call has closed, so the actionable move is positioning for 2028: write to info.tourisme@visitmons.be asking to be notified when the next appel à candidatures opens, and send the portfolio now so it sits with the programming team before the call. Past cycles launched the call in spring/early summer for a following-January festival, so April-July is the window. Mons is small enough that a direct approach reaches the decision-maker; CARACAScom (info@caracascom.com, +32 2 560 21 22) handles their press and can tell you who runs artistic selection. A 4.5-minute drone-and-acrobat finale over the Grand-Place would be genuinely novel for a festival that has been installation-led.
newOpportunities.warning: No 2028 call published yet; the spring/early-summer launch timing is inferred from the 2027 cycle. The artistic selection contact is not named publicly.

newOpportunities.name: Lichtfestival Gent — curated light-art commissions
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Five nights in late January / early February, triennial — next edition 2027
newOpportunities.what: One of Europe's largest city light festivals, run directly by the City of Ghent. The 2024 edition presented 32 light artworks across the medieval centre from local, national and international artists over five nights. It has never run a public open call — works are selected by the city's festival team and invited curators, with roughly half the programme given to locally-connected artists and partnerships. Scale + municipal budget + no open call is precisely the high-value target.
newOpportunities.selection: Curated and invited by Stad Gent's festival service under the Schepen van Feesten, with co-creation partnerships built in. Announced to press roughly two months before the edition.
newOpportunities.scale: ~32 artworks, five nights, full historic city centre, one of the biggest light-festival audiences in the Benelux
newOpportunities.requirements: Dutch or English. Works must handle a Flemish winter and dense crowd flow through narrow medieval streets. Their programme leans installation and projection; a drone show would need a Belgian operator and a site with clear airspace (Portus Ganda / Handelsdok is the plausible one to name).
newOpportunities.intel: Because it is a municipal service rather than a festival company, the way in is the City's culture and festivities administration, not a submissions inbox. Start with pers@stad.gent (09 266 52 37) to be routed to the Lichtfestival programming team, referencing the Schepen van Feesten's cabinet — Melissa Van Houtte in that cabinet was the named press contact for the 2024 edition. Note the triennial rhythm: 2018, 2021, 2024, 2027. The 2027 programme is effectively closed, so you are pitching for 2030 — which means a portfolio arriving in 2028 is early rather than late, and that is the only way into a festival with no call. Propose a Ghent partner (a university lab, a local circus school) and your odds change materially.
newOpportunities.warning: No artistic director or curator is publicly named; the 2024 press contacts may no longer hold those roles. The triennial cadence and 2027 date are confirmed by the festival site, but 2027 dates are not yet published.

newOpportunities.name: Dutch Design Week — Grand Projects open call
newOpportunities.org: Dutch Design Foundation with Bureau Binnenstad Eindhoven
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Nine days in late October annually (DDW 2026: 17-25 October)
newOpportunities.what: DDW is the largest design event in Northern Europe (~350,000 visitors). The Grand Projects open call specifically funds large works in Eindhoven's prime public spaces: a shared pot of EUR100,000 across up to eight projects, waived participation fee, premium locations, permit assistance, a dedicated contact person, partial production funding and full promotional support. One of the few genuinely published, cash-backed calls in the Benelux for large interactive objects in public space.
newOpportunities.selection: Open call with jury; applications close mid-March with decisions by end of April. Separate from the general DDW call for entries which opens around April.
newOpportunities.scale: Nine-day festival, ~350,000 visitors, city-centre public space
newOpportunities.requirements: Framed for designers, architects and researchers rather than performance artists, so lead with the sphere as a public-space interactive object, not the drone show. Partial funding only — you need co-funding, realistically a US grant or a Dutch partner. Nine-day outdoor October run in Dutch weather.
newOpportunities.intel: Apply in the January-March window; the general DDW call for entries opens around April as the fallback route to presence without funding. They assign a dedicated contact person and handle permits, so this is an unusually low-friction first foothold in the Netherlands — and being in Eindhoven during DDW in October puts you in front of GLOW's and STRP's networks in the same city, which is worth more than the fee. A door-opener, not a payday.
newOpportunities.warning: The EUR100,000 / eight-projects figure and the mid-March deadline are from the current call page; the next cycle's exact deadline and whether non-EU applicants are eligible are not explicitly stated.

newOpportunities.name: Yuejin Lantern Festival — Yuejin Supernova proposal open call
newOpportunities.org: Yue Art Museum / Tainan City Cultural Affairs Bureau
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Late Jan - mid Mar annually (Lunar New Year to Lantern Festival)
newOpportunities.what: Taiwan's most design-respected lantern festival — ~14 years running, c.400 works to date, works sited ON and around the Yuejin Harbour water channel in Yanshui. The Yuejin Supernova strand is the open-call track: new light/kinetic/interactive works floated on or bridging the water, plus a new painted boat-house category for 2027. Runs ~6-7 weeks with very high night footfall.
newOpportunities.selection: Written proposal + portfolio reviewed by a curatorial panel convened by Yue Art Museum; shortlist produces on site with technical support from the Cultural Affairs Bureau's contractor.
newOpportunities.scale: City-scale waterfront festival, several hundred thousand visitors per edition, 40+ works
newOpportunities.requirements: Proposal document, concept drawings, budget, CV/portfolio, technical/structural plan. Works must survive outdoor water-adjacent siting for ~7 weeks. Traditional Chinese submission is the norm — partner with a Taiwanese fabricator or translator.
newOpportunities.intel: The 2027 call launched June 2026 with a deadline around 4 Sep 2026, so that cycle has closed — the value is that it recurs on a fixed rhythm: guidelines drop late May/early June, close early September, festival opens the following Lunar New Year. Set a reminder for mid-May 2027 and write to Yue Art Museum (yuejinartmuseum@gmail.com / +886-6-632-4453) in March-April introducing the kinetic-light and interactive-sphere work BEFORE the call opens; the museum shapes each year's themed strands and has previously added categories. The water siting is the differentiator: pitch a floating or reflected kinetic light object, not a drone show. Drone work is contracted separately by the Cultural Affairs Bureau.
newOpportunities.warning: The 2027 deadline was reported in Chinese-language press as 4 Sep 2026; the organiser's own PDF guidelines were blocked by robots.txt so the exact date and whether non-Taiwanese applicants are eligible are unconfirmed. The call text names emerging artists and college teams, which may in practice favour Taiwan-based applicants.

newOpportunities.name: Taiwan Lantern Festival 2027 (Miaoli) — lantern zone & show procurement
newOpportunities.org: Miaoli County Government with Tourism Administration, MOTC
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Feb-Mar 2027, approx. two weeks around Lantern Festival
newOpportunities.what: Taiwan's national-scale roving lantern festival — a different county hosts each year (2026 Chiayi, 2027 Miaoli, theme Between Mountain and Sea, Slow City Glow). Millions of visitors. Content is bought as separately tendered packages: main lantern, themed lantern zones, friendship-city zone, light-environment design, art installations, nightly drone shows and stage performance. The single largest concentration of drone-show and large light-object money in Taiwan.
newOpportunities.selection: Public procurement via the government e-procurement site and the county bidding portal, best-value evaluation by a nine-member committee weighing concept, prior experience and price — not lowest bid.
newOpportunities.scale: National festival, tens of hectares of lantern zones, multi-million-visitor attendance, multiple nightly drone shows
newOpportunities.requirements: Tender documents purchased in person or by mail (~NT$300); bid in Traditional Chinese; nearly always requires a Taiwan-registered company or JV. A US team realistically enters as the named creative subcontractor on a local prime's bid.
newOpportunities.intel: Do NOT try to bid as a US entity. The route is to be named as the international creative partner on a Taiwanese production company's bid — the evaluation committee scores international credentials favourably. Proof the channel is live: Miaoli County posted a 2027 friendship-city lantern zone package at NT$2.5m, bids due 3 Aug 2026, contact Liu Chih-chun, +886-37-558313, mlh0817@ems.miaoli.gov.tw. More 2027 packages are still to come, and the 2028 host county will be announced by MOTC in the same cycle. Watch the Miaoli bidding portal monthly, and email 3-4 Taiwanese lantern-festival primes (the firms credited on 2026 Chiayi) offering the drone choreography + aerialist + LED-costume package as a bid differentiator.
newOpportunities.warning: The NT$2.5m package verified here closed 3 Aug 2026. Further 2027 packages are expected but no specific open one was confirmed as of this scan.

gates.residency: Taiwan-registered entity or JV effectively required

newOpportunities.name: Christmasland in New Taipei City — main show, light zones and circus programming
newOpportunities.org: Tourism and Travel Department, New Taipei City Government
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Mid-Nov to early Jan annually; the 2026 edition opened 14 Nov 2026
newOpportunities.what: Taiwan's biggest winter city festival — roughly seven weeks of building-scale projection mapping, LED light zones and nightly stage programming around Banqiao station, with IP tie-ins and, from the 2025 edition, a circus carnival as the headline show. That circus pivot is the opening: aerial + LED costuming + drones is exactly the register the city has just committed to.
newOpportunities.selection: City procurement and direct commissioning by the Tourism and Travel Department, executed through appointed event production companies; specialty acts are booked as subcontracts to the main show producer.
newOpportunities.scale: ~7 weeks, multi-million attendance, the largest Christmas event in Taiwan
newOpportunities.requirements: Chinese-language contracting; cool, occasionally wet winter conditions; booking via a Taiwanese production prime. Indoor/covered plaza options exist for the sphere.
newOpportunities.intel: Two doors. (1) The main show: find the production company credited on the 2025/2026 circus carnival and pitch a 4.5-minute drone + aerialist finale as a nightly or weekend-peak set piece — the best drone-plus-acrobat fit in the territory because the city has already bought circus. (2) The light zones: the interactive sphere as a plaza anchor. Procurement is visible on the New Taipei City Procurement Office portal (cop.ntpc.gov.tw); tenders for a November opening run March through June. General route: newtaipei.travel/zh-tw/contact-us, or the city switchboard +886-2-2960-3456.
newOpportunities.warning: No named individual officer — the department publishes a contact form rather than programme staff emails. Producer credits for the 2026 circus show were not verifiable from the official site.

newOpportunities.name: Light up Macao — International Light Festival installations and shows
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Early Dec to mid Jan annually (2025 edition: 6 Dec 2025 - 11 Jan 2026)
newOpportunities.what: Macao's flagship winter light festival — 28 installation sets across three districts in the 2025 edition, plus a 6-minute 3D projection mapping show on the Macao Grand Prix Museum running every 15 minutes nightly, carnival zones and shuttle routes. MGTO uses it explicitly as night-economy policy, so budgets are real and the documented appetite for new formats (drones over Nam Van Lake, interactive objects in the Northern District) is on the record.
newOpportunities.selection: Two tracks. International installation and show content is bought by MGTO through procurement and direct commissioning of production companies. Separately there is a local projection-design competition (prizes up to MOP 250,000) restricted to Macao residents 18+.
newOpportunities.scale: 5-6 weeks, 28+ installation sets, three districts, city-wide tourism campaign
newOpportunities.requirements: The resident-only competition is not a route for a US team. The international route requires responding to MGTO tenders or being named on a Macao/HK production company's bid; bilingual documentation.
newOpportunities.intel: Ignore the design competition — Macao-residents-only and the prize money is a red herring for a US studio. Go at MGTO's procurement and partnership side: mgto@macaotourism.gov.mo, +853 2831 5566, and the DST press/partnership pages. The pitch that lands is the one MGTO's own releases are already asking for — nighttime economy in the Northern District and Nam Van Lake, where they have been extending the festival footprint. A 4.5-minute drone show over Nam Van Lake, and the interactive sphere as a Northern District anchor, map directly onto the two things they said they wanted. Pitch May-August: the December festival is scoped and contracted over the summer and announced in late October/November.
newOpportunities.warning: The festival's own microsite could not be loaded (redirect loop) and no tender document for international suppliers was confirmed; the international commissioning route is inferred from MGTO press releases, not a published call.

gates.residency: USA-ok for commissioned work; local competition is Macao-residents-only

newOpportunities.name: Macao International Parade — overseas performing troupes
newOpportunities.org: Cultural Affairs Bureau, Macao SAR Government
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Late March annually (2026 edition: 29 March 2026), plus outreach in the preceding weeks
newOpportunities.what: A government-produced city-scale parade running from a heritage square through the Macao peninsula to a finale stage, built almost entirely from invited international performing troupes alongside local groups. Costumed, illuminated, choreographed street performance in the evening — LED costuming, stilt/aerial rigs and spectacle acts are the core vocabulary. Curated around an annual theme.
newOpportunities.selection: Curatorial invitation by the Cultural Affairs Bureau's events division. No public open call; troupes are scouted from festival circuits, embassy/cultural-institute recommendations, and direct submissions of show reels held on file.
newOpportunities.scale: City-wide evening parade plus finale spectacle, tens of thousands of street spectators, national TV coverage
newOpportunities.requirements: A self-contained touring act of 2-6 performers that reads at street distance at night; travel, visas and freight typically covered for invited troupes; the act must work while moving or in short stops along a route, plus a finale-stage version.
newOpportunities.intel: The strongest fit in the territory for the LED-costume + aerial side of the practice, and it has never had an open call — exactly the kind of target worth a cold pitch. Send a 90-second night-shot reel (not a deck) to the Cultural Affairs Bureau, +853 2836 6866, webmaster@icm.gov.mo, addressed to the parade programme team at the Bureau building, Tap Seac Square. Pitch September-December: the parade is announced publicly in January/February for a late-March event, so troupe selection happens in the autumn. Second, cheaper door: Macao's integrated resorts (SJM, Galaxy, MGM) host parade-linked outreach performances, so a resort entertainment contact can put you in front of the Bureau with a local co-signer.
newOpportunities.warning: No named programme officer published — the Bureau lists only a general webmaster address and switchboard. Fees for invited troupes are not published.

newOpportunities.name: GalaxyArt — Galaxy Macau contemporary installation programme
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Year-round, exhibitions typically 2-4 months; heaviest around Art Macao (Jul-Oct in biennale years) and Lunar New Year
newOpportunities.what: A permanent 6,500+ sq ft free-admission contemporary art venue on the Galaxy Promenade, open since 2021, programming digital and immersive installations, large-scale sculptural work and media art. Galaxy also mounts pavilion exhibitions for Art Macao, where the integrated resorts each stage a major international commission.
newOpportunities.selection: Pure curatorial invitation and direct commission. No open call has ever been published. Works arrive through the venue's curatorial team, through galleries and producers Galaxy already works with, and through the Art Macao resort-pavilion programme coordinated with the Cultural Affairs Bureau.
newOpportunities.scale: 6,500+ sq ft indoor venue in one of the world's highest-footfall resort complexes; Art Macao pavilions run larger
newOpportunities.requirements: Indoor, gallery-grade installation; the 2m interactive sphere is a direct fit for the high-ceilinged main hall. Works must be robust to continuous public interaction over months and to a mass tourist audience with no art-world framing.
newOpportunities.intel: The highest-value cold-pitch target in this list: a genuine commissioner with real money that has never run an open call. Two routes. (1) Direct: Galaxy Entertainment Group's corporate communications and brand marketing team commissions GalaxyArt — approach via Galaxy Macau's corporate enquiry channel, asking specifically for the GalaxyArt curatorial team. (2) Better: route through the Cultural Affairs Bureau's Art Macao coordination (artmacao@icm.gov.mo, +853 8791 9892) — the Bureau pairs international projects with resort pavilions, and being on their radar is how a US studio lands in a Galaxy or MGM space without an existing Macao relationship. Art Macao runs biennially; the 2027 edition's curatorial work begins in late 2026, so this autumn and winter is the window. Same approach works for MGM Cotai's art programme and the Poly MGM Museum.
newOpportunities.warning: GalaxyArt publishes no artist-submission process and no named curator or department contact on its own page; both contact routes are general corporate channels. The Art Macao collateral-exhibition open call is restricted to Macao-registered entities and residents — only the invited/pavilion track is open to a US team.

newOpportunities.name: Swire Properties Arts Month — citywide commissioned installations
newOpportunities.eventWindow: March annually, timed to Art Basel Hong Kong; individual works often run longer
newOpportunities.what: A citywide March commissioning programme across Swire's Hong Kong portfolio — Taikoo Place and ArtisTree, Cityplaza, Pacific Place, Starstreet Precinct, One Island East, EAST Hong Kong and the Upper House. The 2026 edition commissioned nine works including Liam Gillick at Cityplaza and Christine Sun Kim at Pacific Place, described by Swire as mixed-media and multisensory. Interactive, sensor-driven and light-based objects sit squarely inside what they buy.
newOpportunities.selection: Curatorial invitation, commissioned directly by Swire Properties' arts and culture team, often with guest curators and galleries. No open call has ever been published.
newOpportunities.scale: Nine-plus commissioned works across six or more Hong Kong sites, timed to the city's peak art-world month
newOpportunities.requirements: Indoor and covered-atrium siting predominates (ArtisTree, mall atria, hotel lobbies) — a strong fit for the sphere and kinetic light objects. Works must survive a month-plus of unsupervised public interaction in commercial space.
newOpportunities.intel: A commissioner with real budgets and no submission route — pitch cold, to the person who actually answers. Janice Yim, Manager, Public Affairs, is the contact Swire publishes on its own Arts Month releases: janiceyim@swireproperties.com, +852 2844 3094; ask her to route you to the arts and culture team that programmes ArtisTree. Lead with ArtisTree specifically — Swire's dedicated art space and the most likely first booking. The commissioning cycle for a March edition runs the preceding June to September; pitching in January is too late. Swire's programme is a template for HK's other landlord-commissioners: Hongkong Land at LANDMARK, K11 Art Foundation at K11 MUSEA and Hysan at Lee Gardens all commission on a similar rhythm with no open calls.
newOpportunities.warning: Janice Yim's role is Public Affairs (media), not curatorial — she is the published door, not the decision-maker. No curatorial staff contact is published. Budgets are not disclosed.

newOpportunities.name: Harbour City — Art & Culture large-scale installation programme
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Year-round, 4-8 week runs; peak slots are Art Basel HK (March), summer, and Christmas/New Year on the Ocean Terminal harbourfront
newOpportunities.what: Hong Kong's highest-footfall harbourfront retail complex runs a continuous, well-funded art programme: large-scale public installations (JR's GIANTS: Rising Up), interactive environments (SNARKITECTURE's BOUNCE), a dedicated exhibition space called Gallery by the Harbour, and a monthly Art in Life strand. It commissions both indoor atrium works and outdoor harbourfront pieces facing the Victoria Harbour skyline.
newOpportunities.selection: Direct commission by Harbour City's marketing and art-programme team, usually via producers and galleries. No open call has ever been published.
newOpportunities.scale: Multiple concurrent installations across a complex receiving well over 100,000 visitors daily
newOpportunities.requirements: Indoor atrium or covered harbourfront siting; works must handle constant unsupervised public interaction and retail-environment safety rules. The sphere and kinetic light objects fit both Gallery by the Harbour and atrium siting.
newOpportunities.intel: Another no-open-call commissioner. The published route is the general enquiry form — use it, but address the message to the Marketing / Art & Culture team by function, and follow up via the Wharf Group corporate line. The SNARKITECTURE BOUNCE precedent is the argument: they have already bought a large interactive object that people touch and photograph, which is precisely the sphere's profile. Best slots are Christmas/New Year on the Ocean Terminal deck (pitch April-July) and the Art Basel HK March window (pitch September-November). A harbourfront drone show is plausible given the sightlines, but Marine Department and CAD airspace approval is the long pole — raise it as a second-phase idea, not the opener.
newOpportunities.warning: No named contact or artist-submission process published on Harbour City's own site; only a general contact form and concierge. Budget range unverified.

newOpportunities.name: WestK (West Kowloon Cultural District) — Freespace & Art Park commissions
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Year-round; outdoor Art Park programming clusters Oct-Dec and Mar-May; Freespace seasons announced twice yearly
newOpportunities.what: Hong Kong's flagship cultural district — a 23-hectare harbourfront site with M+, the Hong Kong Palace Museum, the Freespace performance venue and a large outdoor Art Park with a harbour-facing lawn used for festivals and large outdoor works. Freespace Tech Lab and the Creation for Freespace series show an explicit institutional appetite for scenography, stage technology and technically ambitious performance. The Art Park lawn is one of very few Hong Kong sites where an outdoor drone show over water is institutionally plausible.
newOpportunities.selection: Two channels. Artistic programming is curated by WestK's performing arts and visual arts teams by invitation and through producer relationships. Production, design and technical services are bought through published tender notices and an expression-of-interest process under Business Opportunities.
newOpportunities.scale: 23-hectare district, harbourfront Art Park, Freespace Box (up to ~900 standing) and The Room
newOpportunities.requirements: For tenders, a registered entity and HK-compliant insurance/safety documentation; for artistic programming, a producer or co-presenting partner is close to essential. Outdoor drone work requires Civil Aviation Department permission plus Authority sign-off.
newOpportunities.intel: Use both doors at once. (1) Register and monitor the Authority's Business Opportunities and Tender Notices / EOI pages — EOIs for festival content and technical production appear there and are the cleanest formal way in for a foreign supplier. (2) In parallel, pitch the Freespace team directly, referencing Freespace Tech Lab and Creation for Freespace by name, because those strands exist to absorb exactly this kind of technology-forward performance. Seasons are announced roughly twice a year, so pitch January-April for the following autumn. The sphere fits an Art Park or Freespace foyer siting during a festival weekend; the drone-plus-aerialist piece is the harbourfront lawn pitch.
newOpportunities.warning: The Authority's tender/EOI pages could not be loaded directly (robots.txt redirect loop) — the URLs and the existence of the Business Opportunities channel are confirmed from the Authority's own domain, but no currently open notice or named programme contact was verified.

newOpportunities.name: Keelung harbour arts programme — Keelung Ciao / Ghost Festival exhibitions
newOpportunities.org: Keelung City Cultural Affairs Bureau with Keelung For A Walk
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Aug-Sep annually for the Ghost Festival strand; Keelung Ciao harbour strand typically Sep-Oct
newOpportunities.what: Keelung runs several overlapping harbour-city art strands: the Keelung Ciao harbour arts festival at the port, the Zhengbin Harbour art village residency, and a city exhibition strand run with local organisation Keelung For A Walk around the century-old Mid-Summer Ghost Festival — the 2026 edition themed on the festival's soundscape, with both an artwork call and an on-site residency with housing provided. Works are sited in harbour buildings and waterfront spaces.
newOpportunities.selection: Open call by email submission — CV, portfolio, concept statement; panel review. Residency applicants must be 20+.
newOpportunities.scale: City-scale harbour festival; individual exhibition venues are modest
newOpportunities.requirements: Email submission to the organiser; contemporary art track record; theme relevance. International artists explicitly welcome.

newOpportunities.eventWindow: Mid-Nov to early Jan (2026 run: Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 2, 2027)

newOpportunities.warning: No published budget figures; moneyTier high is inferred from the exhibition's scale and ticketed model. No named exhibitions-department contact is published — the PR contact is a routing step, not the decision-maker.

No staff emails are published — call (316) 660-0600 and ask for Masterson by name, then follow with a one-page deck. Only a general line is published — 701 Market Street Suite 1250, 314-881-2015 — so call and ask for whoever leads events/programming, then send a one-pager naming the NYE slot explicitly. newOpportunities.name: Minnesota State Fair — entertainer submissions & Arts A'Fair
newOpportunities.eventWindow: Twelve days ending Labor Day (late Aug - early Sept)

Arts A'Fair takes performing-arts proposals in early 2027 at artsafair@mnstatefair.org / 651-288-4395; pitch the LED-costumed acrobatic work there as a performing-arts commission rather than a midway act, because the money and the artistic framing are better. newOpportunities.warning: Deadline null — the fair publishes a submissions-open date (after Oct 1) but no closing date. No fee or pay range is published anywhere on the fair's site.

newOpportunities.what: Lagos State's government-produced festive-season spectacle: a three-day, multi-site fiesta with a New Year's Eve countdown that has previously used large-scale fireworks and aerial display on the Eko Atlantic waterfront. Commissioned entirely by the ministry and its appointed producers — no open call has ever existed. Lagos is West Africa's largest spectacle market and Detty December has turned the last ten days of the year into a continental draw.
newOpportunities.selection: Appointed by the Ministry or the Special Adviser's office, usually through a Nigerian production company; state procurement rules apply above threshold.
newOpportunities.scale: Multiple simultaneous venues across Lagos; countdown audiences in the hundreds of thousands plus national broadcast
newOpportunities.requirements: Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority drone permits (slow — start 3+ months out); local production partner effectively mandatory; a Nigerian corporate co-sponsor materially improves the odds.
newOpportunities.intel: The ministry is the client but the practical route is the sponsor: Lagos countdown production is heavily underwritten by telecoms and banks, and a sponsor-funded drone finale is an easier sell than a line item in the state budget. Approach the Commissioner's office (Hon. Toke Benson-Awoyinka) in writing by June with a costed 4.5-minute waterfront drone sequence, and simultaneously approach Eko Atlantic's events team, which controls the countdown site. Art X Lagos (November) and the Lagos Biennial are the culture-side warm-up visits that make the December pitch credible.
newOpportunities.warning: Lagos cancelled the Greater Lagos Fiesta for the 2025/26 turn of the year and redirected to prayer gatherings — the event is not guaranteed to run in any given year. No ministry email, phone or procurement page is published on the official site; contact must be established by letter or intermediary. Fee levels unverified.

newOpportunities.what: South Africa's principal art-and-technology festival, founded 2014 and run out of Wits University's Tshimologong precinct in Braamfontein. It programmes digital and new-media art, interactive installation, performance-with-technology and an awards strand, and explicitly convenes African and international creatives, technologists, researchers and innovators. The natural continental home for the interactive sphere and kinetic light objects.
newOpportunities.selection: Curated by the festival director's team, with periodic open calls (an awards open call has run publicly); installation slots are largely invited.
newOpportunities.scale: Five-day festival across the Braamfontein precinct; regional art-tech audience plus academic and industry delegates
newOpportunities.requirements: Indoor precinct venues; 220V; works need to survive public student-quarter footfall. Shipping into South Africa needs an ATA carnet or temporary-import arrangement.
newOpportunities.intel: A relationship festival, not a submissions festival — email hello@fakugesi.co.za and ask for Festival Director Alby Michaels by name, with a short video of the sphere rather than a proposal PDF. Pitch as a co-presentation: Fak'ugesi has a documented history of mobility partnerships with the British Council's East Africa Arts programme, and a Goethe-Institut Johannesburg or US Mission South Africa cultural-grant co-funder makes the budget work where the festival's own fee will not reach this artist's range. The realistic play is Fak'ugesi as the anchor that unlocks a two-week South African tour (V&A Waterfront, Cape Town Carnival) on one shipping cost.
newOpportunities.warning: The festival's own site does not publish installation open-call terms, deadlines, artist fees or international-eligibility rules — the contact is confirmed, the process is not. Budget is almost certainly below the $9k sphere floor without a co-funder.

newOpportunities.eventWindow: Rolling. Municipal festive-lighting, New Year and heritage-celebration packages cluster in Aug-Oct advertising for Nov-Jan delivery
newOpportunities.what: The single statutory portal carrying every tender from every South African public-sector body at national, provincial and municipal level — searchable by organ of state, province and status. newOpportunities.scale: Metro-scale; the eight South African metros each run seasonal lighting and activation budgets
newOpportunities.requirements: South African supplier registration on the Central Supplier Database is required to bid — a US team almost always enters as a named subcontractor or JV partner to a registered local bidder. B-BBEE scoring materially disadvantages a foreign-only bid.

Set a weekly search on the portal filtered to Currently Advertised with the keywords festive lighting, activation, events management and fireworks across the metros, then approach the local firms who win those packages and offer the drone/acrobat and LED-sphere modules as a subcontract line — the same pattern that works with the big US drone primes.
